deepdive.sec: Auto components — metal/chassis & safety systems (+ emerging aerospace/defense precision mfg)

bull_bear.body:
- M&A discipline: targets chosen on customers / capabilities / verticalization; pay "mild" multiples. Mag Filter & SDM at ~book value; Chester Hall & H-One at mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA. All four EPS- and ROCE-accretive from day one.
- **QIP:** enabling resolution up to INR2,000 cr (purpose not yet specified — debt repay / acquisition TBD).
- Merger of Badve Autocomps & Eximius into listco at ~book value (group simplification).
- Final dividend INR0.55/share. Net debt INR5,977mn; ROCE 14.7%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Oil-crisis cost inflation (fuel, transport, labor, personnel); Haryana minimum-wage hike — pass-through partial/lagged, transport unresolved.
- Commodity volatility (mitigated by back-to-back pricing but with lag).
- Aerospace execution: SDM startup losses, long certification lead times (12-24 months), integration risk.
- Customer concentration legacy (historically single-customer dependent; now diversified).
- Trading business margin dilution.
- Chassis wins partly cannibalize existing business.
- QIP dilution risk (up to INR2,000 cr, undefined use).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and delivery-focused; emphasized hitting all five FY26 commitments. Candid on Q4 cost headwinds but framed as one-time/short-term. Declined plant-level utilization/break-even, segment-level revenue (suspension/polymer, H-One), and QIP use specifics — guarded on granular numbers.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Steering column was a 3-decade single-supplier monopoly Belrise broke via engineering — the wedge that won the fastest-growing 2W/3W OEM.
- Stainless-steel surface-coating/plating for premium exhausts is a near-unique domestic capability (competitive moat).
- 850+ robots fleet + full verticalization (tooling→stamping→fabrication→painting/coating→assembly) underpins exhaust cost edge.
- Aerospace M&A is really about buying certifications/customer access (otherwise 2-3 yr + 12-24 month qualification) to then shift work to India ("best-cost," not low-cost).
- Chester Hall: GBP18.5mn rev, GBP2.1mn EBITDA, >20% ROCE, single-source reverse-thruster/nacelle parts, top-5 quality at engine OEM, titanium/Al-grade-7 machining, 0.5-1% rejection.
- Content-per-vehicle INR20k figure includes the Badve Autocomps + Eximius merger.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

business.body: 2W/3W dominant (~82% mfg rev) and structurally favored — segment only just regained pre-COVID peak, leaving headroom. 4W/CV small but blue-ocean, growing fast (H-One lifted 4W content INR25k→40-45k). Aerospace/defense nascent but strategic, built entirely via M&A (SDM France + Chester Hall UK). Trading business is margin-dilutive; possible localization/hive-off discussed but no decision.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The deck's headline claim is that "Hyva India's Tipper Business: catalyzing Belrise's role as a Tier-0.5 Supplier" — the transaction is positioned as a step up the supplier tier rather than a bolt-on.
- The acquired business "Serves all of the top 5 commercial vehicle OEMs" and is described as a "Design and development partner to all key commercial vehicle OEMs".
- Deck states the deal "Adds a leading European commercial vehicle OEM to Belrise's customer base"; the OEM is not named.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Belrise has entered a Business Transfer Agreement to acquire the India Tipper Body business of Hyva (India) Pvt. Ltd. — a subsidiary of JOST Werke SE — on a slump sale basis.
- [Deal terms] "Purchase Consideration: $5.65M USD", described as "Acquired at ~3.60x EV/EBITDA", where per footnotes the Enterprise Value "has been computed on a cash-free, debt-free basis" and the valuation "is based on EBITDA for CY25, derived from management accounts".
- [Target economics] Deck cites "Est. EBITDA CY25: ~1.57M USD" and "ROCE: ~20%" for CY25, defined as January to December 2025, with a footnote assuming a USD/INR exchange rate of 95.26.
- [Disclosure route] Presentation filed with BSE (Scrip Code 544405) and NSE (Symbol BELRISE), ISIN INE894V01022, under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA 11.4% (Q4) / 12.1% (FY26); mfg EBITDA 13.0% / 13.7%. Back-to-back RM pricing (steel, plastic) passes input cost moves to customers with a lag → stable gross margins. Q4 pressured by one-time INR94.7mn SDM startup loss + acquisition legal/professional fees + oil-crisis-driven fuel/transport/labor/personnel costs (Haryana min-wage). Fuel & labor to be passed on over time; transport still under OEM discussion. Mgmt expects no material medium/long-term margin impact.
latest_quarter.title: Margins

latest_quarter.body: First structured note for BELRISE in this system (FY26 = first full year post-May-2025 IPO). Baseline established. Key new-this-quarter items: Chester Hall UK acquisition closed (Q4 FY26); SDM one-time INR94.7mn startup loss; QIP enabling resolution up to INR2,000 cr announced; Badve Autocomps + Eximius merger Board-approved; new 2W exhaust/fuel-tank orders (~INR310 cr combined peak); EV chassis/battery-tray order; 650cc Italian export single-source win. Compare against next quarter.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- Continued **mid-teens revenue growth**.
- **EBITDA margins broadly stable** vs FY26 levels.
- **Capex 6%–6.5% of manufacturing revenue** (R&D included within this).
- Double 4W+CV business over 2 years; needs ~40-45% growth vs FY25 base this fiscal.
- Belrise SDM expected EBITDA-positive in CY2027 (one-time INR94.7mn startup loss in Q4 not recurring).
- Aerospace targeted to grow into a >10% revenue contributor over time.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- **2W/3W OEM (fastest-growing):** new order for exhaust systems + fuel tanks for top-selling model; Bangalore brownfield, production from Q2 FY27, peak revenue ~INR90 cr. Built from earlier steering-column + suspension programs (broke 3-decade monopoly on steering columns).
- **Japanese 2W OEM:** 8-week rescue of distressed Tier-1 led to large order for complete exhaust systems + metal components for highest-selling model; peak ~INR220 cr (~INR2,000mn), production from Q4 FY27. (Combined #1+#2 = ~INR310 cr peak.)
- **Haridwar facility** ramping; trial parts dispatched to largest 2W OEM; fed by Greater Noida & Pantnagar (backward integration, limited greenfield capex).
- **Chassis** wins for new marquee model launches at a top customer's Pune & Sambhajinagar plants (partly replacement).
- **EV:** chassis, battery trays + metal components for an emerging EV player (in partnership with a large Japanese 2W OEM); supplies from Q3 FY27.
- **Premium export:** single-source component order for a 650cc Italian OEM premium motorbike (low volume, high complexity, only one other domestic supplier capable).
- Proprietary segment marquee customer adds: suspensions +4, steering columns +4, high-tensile +4, braking +2.
outlook.title: Order book / new wins

outlook.body:
- Content-per-vehicle expansion (2W +60-65%, of which ~80% proprietary in-house products) + cross-selling each new product to 3-4 OEMs.
- New 2W OEM penetration (two large fast-growers from near-zero base → "very large" in 2-3 yrs).
- 4W/CV model wins via H-One high-tensile (up to 1,200 MPa domestic / 1,700 MPa via H-One global) enabling lightweighting & safety.
- GST rate cut demand stimulus (hope structural, not pull-forward).
- Aerospace India localization (China+1, captive Indian aircraft demand, 8-11 yr aircraft backlogs, certification moats acquired via M&A).
outlook.title: Growth drivers

deepdive.thesis: Belrise is a diversified 2W/3W metal & plastics leader (exhaust, fuel tanks, chassis) compounding via three levers: rising content-per-vehicle (2W ~INR12k→20k over 18 months, +60-65%), proprietary segment wins (suspensions, steering columns, high-tensile, braking), and a cheap-multiple M&A strategy now opening a high-complexity aerospace/defense leg aimed at India localization. Back-to-back RM pricing protects gross margins; FY26 delivered guided mid-teens growth with stable margins.

Post-merger, net of related-party eliminations, expect an incremental INR10 billion (INR1,000 crore) of revenue added to Belrise plus a margin uplift, and ~30% higher wallet share in plastics with marquee OEMs.
Brownfield expansion at Bangalore facility for a fast-growing 2W/3W OEM (exhaust systems and fuel tanks) with production slated to begin Q2FY27 and peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Secured first order (plastic-molded parts) under the GPA with a leading electric 2W OEM, to be catered from Aurangabad, with supplies expected to commence Q2FY2027.
Secured orders for chassis, battery trays and other metal components for an emerging EV player (with a large Japanese 2W OEM), with supplies expected to commence Q3FY27.
Expect to continue delivering mid-teens revenue growth, consistent with track record and order-book momentum.
Reiterated aim to double four-wheeler and commercial vehicle revenue versus FY25, requiring ~40-45% growth this fiscal (FY26 4W grew 37%, CV grew 35%).
Expect the one-time operational loss (INR94.7 million in Q4FY26) in Belrise Aerospace and Defense (SDM, France) to be non-recurring and SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

Haridwar facility ramp-up progressing well with trial parts already dispatched to a large 2W OEM; expect to reach peak production over FY27, fed by Greater Noida and Pantnagar facilities to limit greenfield capex.
Major new order from a large Japanese 2W OEM for complete exhaust systems and metal components, expected peak annual revenue ~INR220 crore with production commencing in Q4FY27.
Expect capex to remain in the range of 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue (inclusive of R&D), reflecting ongoing capacity and capability investments.
Expect EBITDA margins to remain broadly stable compared to FY26 levels (FY26 EBITDA margin 12.1%).
SDM (French aerospace acquisition) expected to generate revenues of approximately EUR3-4 million in FY27; acquired at consideration of EUR0.35 million (~0.1x sales).
Maintained capex guidance of INR8,000 million over this fiscal year and the next fiscal year, no change from prior quarter.
Guided for capex of up to INR8,000 million over the next two fiscal years, largely funded through internal accruals (~INR400 crore/year).
Expect H-One subsidiary to double revenue (with little or no capex) to INR400-450 crore (INR4,000-4,500 million) over the next 24 months from ~INR60 crore/quarter today.

Expect two newly-won two-wheeler customers (a fast-growing 2W/3W OEM via Bangalore and a large Japanese OEM at ~INR200 crore) to grow from negligible contribution today to very large customers over the next two to three years.

Expect near-term cost pressures (oil crisis, fuel, labour, transportation, Haryana minimum wage) to be short-term with no material impact on medium-to-long-term margins; will pass fuel and labour costs to customers over time, transportation still under discussion.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
